name: Nicaragua
sources: NICARAGUA HAS NO USABLE DOLLAR GDP FOR 1990 AND THIS FILE DOES NOT PRETEND OTHERWISE. THE ENTERED 2.8 IS A RECONSTRUCTION, NOT A TRANSCRIPTION, AND HERE IS EXACTLY WHAT WAS DONE. The World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.CD series for NIC prints $2,082m for 1989, $519m for 1990 and $3,678m for 1991 — down 75% and then up sevenfold — while real GDP moved by roughly -0.1% and -0.2% across the same two years. Nothing happened to Nicaraguan output in 1990; what happened was the córdoba. Inflation ran in the thousands of percent, the official rate was administered and multiple, and the currency was replaced twice (the córdoba of February 1988 and the córdoba oro of 1991) before a market-clearing rate existed. Entering the $519m print would have made Nicaragua the poorest country on earth in 1990 at $125 a head — poorer than Mozambique, which is false — and would then have propagated through every ratio in this file, because debt, military spending and oil are all divided by it. The figure entered is the geometric mean of the two adjacent prints of the same series, sqrt(2082 x 3678) = $2,767m, rounded to 2.8, which is what the series itself says the economy was worth on either side of a year in which real output did not move. It gives $675 per head, which is a plausible 1990 Nicaragua and is roughly what later reconstructions put it at. UNVERIFIED. If a later agent finds a rebased series, this is the first number in the file to replace.

Population 4.15m: World Bank SP.POP.TOTL, series NIC, 1990 = 4,152,000 on the UN World Population Prospects basis the series uses. Softer than it looks: the census of 1995 enumerated 4,357,099, which back-cast at the period's growth rate gives something nearer 3.8m for 1990, and the gap is the undercount adjustment the UN applies to a country that had just come out of a war with a fifth of its population displaced. Entered at the series figure for roster consistency; 3.8m is the enumerated lower bound.

INFLATION 2.95 IS A CEILING, NOT A MEASUREMENT. Nicaraguan CPI inflation in 1990 was about 3,004% — 30.04 in this file's fraction-of-1 units, ten times what data/mod.rs will accept and what economy.rs clamps to on the first tick. The band exists because the demand channel is linear and unbounded in the distance from neutral, so a true figure here sends GDP through zero and takes the suite with it; the schema's own error message says to enter what the model can carry and record the real print, which is what this does. For scale, the same series reads 4,775% for 1988 and 7,429% for 1989 and then 117% for 1991 — Violeta Chamorro's stabilisation, which the sim has to find on its own and which is not scripted anywhere. interest_rate 2.9 is a stand-in on the same grounds, entered a shade under the clamped inflation exactly as Brazil, Peru and Argentina are, so the row opens at monetary neutral rather than with a fabricated real rate driving growth in either direction.

system Command and tax 25%: the Sandinista state owned the banks, the export trade, the mines and about a fifth of the land after the confiscations, and the Area Propiedad del Pueblo ran the rest through licensing. A tax figure for such a state is a statement about how much of output the budget moved rather than a revenue ratio in the market sense, and 0.25 is entered on the same convention Cuba's 0.55 is. FLAGGED as a convention, not a print.

MILITARY SPENDING 25% OF GDP IS THE LEAST RELIABLE NUMBER IN THIS FILE AND IS THE HARDEST CALL IN THE BRANCH. SIPRI's Military Expenditure Database carries $1,142m current dollars for Nicaragua in 1990 and — this is the tell — carries no share-of-GDP figure for that year at all, because there was no GDP to divide it by. SIPRI's first share figure is 4.0% for 1991, after the war ended, the army was cut and the currency was replaced. $1,142m against the 2.8 reconstructed above would be 41% of GDP, and against the $519m print 220%. What is not in doubt is the magnitude of the thing being paid for: the Ejercito Popular Sandinista had something over 70,000 regulars under a universal draft in a country of four million, the largest force ever raised on the isthmus, and defence had been taking a quarter to a third of Nicaraguan output through the late 1980s. 0.25 is entered at the bottom of the defensible band, because demobilisation ordered under the Tela accord of August 1989 had already begun and because this field is read as a sustained burden rather than a wartime peak. It is a judgement and it is labelled one.

Strength 7 sits far above what the budget above can buy at this GDP, on the same grounds cuba.json states for its own 12 and for Israel: the arsenal was given, not purchased. The EPS in January 1990 had on the order of 100 T-55s, BM-21 rocket artillery, Mi-24 and Mi-17 helicopters and an air defence network, all Soviet-supplied — the only heavy force between Mexico and Colombia. Indexed just below Mexico's 8 and above Colombia's 7 on equipment and combat experience rather than headcount. The model will decay it toward what the economy sustains once the patron stops paying, and that is not a defect: the EPS went from over 70,000 to about 15,000 between 1990 and 1993, and this is the mechanism that should produce it.

DEBT 3.8 IS REAL AND IS THE HIGHEST RATIO IN THE ROSTER. External debt at end-1990 was on the order of $10.5-11bn against the $2.8bn above — the highest debt-to-output ratio in the world at the time, and unserviceable by any arithmetic. Roughly a third of it was owed to the Soviet Union and the CMEA in transferable roubles whose dollar value neither side ever agreed, which is the same caveat cuba.json carries and for the same reason. This crosses the 0.9 debt-drag threshold in economy.rs by a wide margin and takes something like six points a year off growth; that is severe and it is the correct severity for a country that could not borrow a dollar until the arrears clearance of 1991. APPROXIMATE in the second digit, certain in the first.

Oil 0.0: no production. The energy base was Soviet crude arriving on concessional terms at a rate of some 15,000 barrels a day, and the withdrawal of it — Moscow cut deliveries sharply across 1990 — is a shock this file cannot express as an oil figure because Nicaragua never produced any. It belongs to the patronage relationship in statecraft and to the USSR line in relations_1990.json.

TFP trend -0.015: the worst in the roster, below Cuba's -0.012. Real output per head in 1990 was roughly at its 1950s level; the economy had contracted in every year but one since 1983 under the combined weight of the war, the United States trade embargo in force since 1 May 1985, the mining of the harbours, and an administered price system that had stopped clearing. The Soviet and CMEA support that was the counterweight was being withdrawn on the same schedule as Cuba's.
Investment 18% of GDP, split 12 public and 6 private: a state-led ratio for a state-owned economy, and most of it maintenance rather than capacity. Reasoned apportionment, not a print.

Stability 30 and authoritarianism 0.50. Three weeks after this file opens, on 25 February 1990, the government lost an election it had called and conceded it — Violeta Chamorro's UNO took 54.7% to Daniel Ortega's 40.8%, against every poll, and the transfer of power took place on 25 April. NOTHING IN THIS FILE ENCODES THAT, and the authoritarianism figure is the place where it would have leaked in if anywhere. 0.50 is below the 0.60 electoral ceiling in government.rs, which means the model treats Nicaragua as a state whose government can be removed by a vote — which is precisely what February 1990 demonstrated it was, and precisely what almost nobody believed in January. Against a lower figure: a vanguard party fused with the state, a universal draft, La Prensa closed for over a year, a state of emergency from 1982 to 1988, and the Coordinadora's boycott of the 1984 election. Stability 30 is the war, the hyperinflation and an army that would shortly have to take orders from the widow of the man it had been founded to avenge.

Separatism 0.15, the highest in this branch by a factor of ten, and it is a real one rather than a sentiment. The Miskito, Sumu and Rama of the Atlantic coast rose against the Sandinista state in 1981-82 after the forced relocations from the Rio Coco, fought alongside the Contras as MISURASATA and then YATAMA, and won: the Autonomy Statute of 7 September 1987 created two autonomous regions covering roughly half the national territory with their own councils. Half the map governed under a separate constitutional arrangement won by armed revolt is a different order of thing from Bolivia's 0.10 or Colombia's 0.10, and 0.15 is where it goes.

pop_growth_1990 = 2.3584%/yr. Compound annual growth of World Bank SP.POP.TOTL, series NIC (Nicaragua): 3,619,104 in 1984 to 4,066,476 in 1989 — the five years ending on the eve of the 1 January 1990 start date. See EconomyRecord::pop_growth_1990 in spheres-sim/src/data/mod.rs for why the window ends in 1989 and not with the single-year 1990 rate.

note: 1990 TECHNOLOGY: AUTHORED, NOT DERIVED. What this nation knew on 1 January 1990 is transcribed and sourced grant by grant, exactly like every other 1990 figure in this file, and is not read off tfp_trend - there was never a code path from the trend to the known set, and the zero that stood there was a claim about the world rather than an absence of one (BIBLE section 8 and iron rule 4, both amended 2026-08-30). THE PREDICATE IS SPLIT, and split by the technology's OWN EFFECT TYPE so that it is mechanically computable and never a per-nation judgement call. A node whose effects include MilitaryEfficiency, MilitaryStrength, DiffusionEmission or CostReduction is SOVEREIGNTY-SIDE: holding it means this nation could PRODUCE it, so operating an imported article does not qualify. Every other node is USE-SIDE: deployed and in operational use here is enough, whoever built it, because the effect such a node pays is a productivity, health or output effect and that effect is real in the country where the machine runs. Of the 48 technologies the tree lets anyone hold in 1990, 17 are sovereignty-side and 31 are use-side.

DATA-KEYED TAIL NATION. This nation is outside the 29 authored majors, so nothing here was authored technology by technology: a grant is made only where one of two named published global series supports it, and nothing is modelled, estimated or interpolated. A short list, or an empty one, is the correct outcome of that rule and not a gap in the work.

Data-keyed tail nation: not one of the 29 authored majors. Only the two series named in ruling 3 were consulted - WHO/UNICEF WUENIC DTP3 1990 and World Bank IT.CEL.SETS. Nothing was modelled, estimated or interpolated, and no other evidence was admitted. ISO3 key used for both series: NIC.
AUTHORED, AND THE ANSWER IS NOTHING. Both named series were checked and both refused this nation; the empty grant list is a finding, not an absence of work.
WUENIC DTP3 1990 = 70% against the 80% UCI-1990 threshold: refused.
IT.CEL.SETS at 31 December 1989 = 0 against a threshold of any positive count: refused.

The other 46 grantable 1990 technologies are BLANK for this nation by design, not by oversight: the 17 sovereignty-side entries are unreachable by any use-in-operation series, and no published global series was named that keys the remaining 29 use-side entries.
